notes:
Attempt 2 is a large, genuine improvement: the shipping-blocker is gone. The stray collar-leaf button that made attempt 1 indistinguishable from the sibling option collar-point-70-btn has been removed, the band buttonhole is back in its drawn position, the edge topstitching is restored on the dominant leaf, and the crop no longer competes with the model's face. A customer could now correctly tell this option apart from its neighbours. What remains are four honest but Minor proportional and finishing drifts - band height, left-leaf stitch continuity, leaf blade width, and a strip of jaw in frame - none of which misrepresent the product, but none of which I can honestly certify at the 98 / under-2-percent-deviation bar the gate requires. Scoring truthfully rather than rounding up.

UPSTREAM DEFECT REQUIRING HUMAN ACTION - this option cannot reliably pass until it is fixed: spec.json for collar-point-70 carries the shape token 'button-down point', a false positive scraped from the description's contrast clause 'the sweet spot between the long traditional point and the casual button-down'. build_prompt.mjs promotes that token into a hard instruction ('Exact specification - button-down point, point shape') and into the QC checklist ('shape reads as drawn: button-down point'), so the locked prompt actively instructs the model to add a collar button the drawing does not have, and the checklist then demands the very feature the blueprint forbids. Attempt 2 only succeeded because an explicit correction block was appended to override it. The fix belongs in the shape extractor in feature-extraction (negate shape tokens that appear inside a comparative or contrastive clause such as 'between X and Y', 'rather than', 'unlike', 'as opposed to'), not in this option's prompt. The same false positive will affect any option whose description names a sibling style for contrast.
